lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience is not newest-first: Crestline appears above the more recent Harbor Payments internship.
items.because: A reader may misread the chronology or question the document’s organization.

items.says: Education appears before Experience.
items.because: Leading with Education may make the more directly relevant work history less visible.

items.says: The current Diesel Mechanic entry is not clearly connected to a product-focused résumé.
items.because: Its relevance is unexplained, and it takes space from product and operations experience.

items.says: The scorecard bullet names recurring work but not what it changed.
items.because: Without an outcome, the value of the work is hard to judge.

items.says: “Owned” describes responsibility rather than action, and “that discussed them” is redundant.
items.because: The wording does not clarify the contribution and uses space unnecessarily.

items.says: The 30% reduction in pick errors has no comparison period or baseline.
items.because: Without an anchor, the result is harder to interpret.

items.says: The forecast-error figures lack a defined metric and comparison periods, and the line does not show that the consensus forecast caused the change.
items.because: Without those details, the figures and attribution are not clearly interpretable.

items.says: The 1,800-hour annual saving has no stated baseline or measurement method.
items.because: A reader may question how the figure was measured and what it is compared against.

items.says: The 1,800-hour saving appears after a long activity list.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the quantified outcome.

items.says: The bullet combines activities without showing which change saved driver hours.
items.because: The link between the work and the hours saved is unclear.

items.says: The line misdefines RICE Reach as support tickets a feature might close.
items.because: Reach estimates people or users affected over a defined period, while tickets measure a support outcome.

items.says: The line does not say what the scoring led you to prioritize.
items.because: Without the resulting priority or decision, the value of the work is hard to judge.

items.says: The line does not identify the loss found or the roadmap priority selected.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the analysis revealed or which product action it supported.

items.says: The checkout-test bullet repeats the preceding bullet’s A/B test and five-point lift.
items.because: It restates the result without adding distinct impact.

items.says: Session-level randomization does not establish an effect on distinct customers.
items.because: Customers can have multiple sessions, so the test supports a session-level effect, not necessarily a customer-level one.

items.says: The claim that all 9 tonnes would otherwise have been thrown away is not established.
items.because: Redistribution shows where the food went, not what would otherwise have happened to it.

items.says: “Launched a surplus-food pickup app” does not say what you did to develop or launch it.
items.because: Without a concrete contribution, your Product Lead role is harder to assess.

items.says: The stated 150% increase is mathematically wrong; growth from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.
items.because: The increase of 750 divided by the starting 400 is 187.5%.

items.says: The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is about 26.7%.

items.says: The $2.4M annual savings estimate does not say how the model was built.
items.because: A key input or analysis would make the consulting contribution easier to judge.

items.says: Passive wording hides your actions in the patient-intake bullet.
items.because: It does not make clear who mapped intake or shortened the form.

items.says: “The final recommendation” does not specify the change approved.
items.because: Readers need to know what the pilot would test.

items.says: The practicum bullets repeat the scheduling-pilot approval or funding outcome.
items.because: The second mention adds little new information and takes space from the work behind the estimate.
